title: A build without optimization and without TRON_AMX_DISPATCH fails to link: advance() calls begin_region/end_region outside the #ifdef
problem: Lines 507 and 509 call amx_attn_h128g4::begin_region() and end_region() outside #ifdef TRON_AMX_DISPATCH. Their definitions are in amx_attn.cpp, which is compiled only with that option (src/tron/CMakeLists.txt:220-221). use_block_kernel is a run-time bool. So only the optimizer removes the two calls. The attention call site keeps the same calls inside the #ifdef (self_attention.hpp:1556-1590). Note [AMX attention dispatch] item 1 says that every dispatch block is excluded without the option. The design text (section 5.6) says the GDN call site is inside the #ifdef.
scenario: Configure a Debug build without the option. The presets coverage, asan and tsan do this (CMakePresets.json), and Debug adds -O0. CI builds the coverage preset (cpp-coverage.yml, make build-coverage). Every binary that instantiates advance() then has undefined references to tron::amx_attn_h128g4::begin_region() and end_region(). Examples are t_gated_delta_net (t_gated_delta_net.cpp:2719) and a plugin with a GDN operation. Evidence: a 20-line copy of the pattern, compiled with g++ 11.4, keeps both references at -O0 and has none at -O2. clang-19 was not available on this machine, so the clang result is inferred: at -O0 clang folds only conditions that are constant expressions, and this one depends on function arguments.
fix: Put lines 505-510 (the begin_region call and the tron::finally that calls end_region) inside #ifdef TRON_AMX_DISPATCH, as self_attention.hpp does.

title: No test runs the refusal fallback of advance() or the counters of full windows
problem: No test reaches the fallback at lines 675-678, the counter update at lines 679-680, or the two full-window branches of the tally (line 540 for the amx path, line 544 for half_full_block_tokens). The executor test of the block path (t_gated_delta_net.cpp:2776-2824) uses finite inputs, the executor with one key head per group, and no tally. The kernel test of refusals (t_amx_gdn_numerics.cpp:304-320) calls the kernel directly and checks only that the matrix is unchanged. The one test that reads the block counters runs a chain of 3 tokens and expects zeros (t_gated_delta_net.cpp:2371-2374).
scenario: Delete the gdn_recurrence_chain_head call, or pass head_of_key in place of value_head. The output rows of a refused value head then keep the kernel's unfinished values, and its matrix stays at the block start. Or swap amx_blocks with amx_fallback_blocks, or delete line 544. Every test still passes. The block path with key_heads_per_group > 1 (the first_head offsets at lines 654-666) is not run by any test either.
fix: Add one executor case at wide_chain_geometry. Start from a checkpoint with one infinity in the matrix of one value head (start_from_checkpoint rejects only NaN). Advance one full window with when_available and a tally. Require the bytes of step() for that head's matrix rows and output columns, the existing band for the other heads, and on an AMX machine amx_fallback_blocks == 1. Add one case that needs no AMX: 32 tokens from position 0 with gdn_block_kernel::off and a tally must give half_full_block_tokens == 32 per key head.

verdict.evidence: /home/jhan/workspace/ai-runs/tron-gdn-amx-review/h/tron/models/gdn_rolling_executor.hpp:675-680 (fallback and block counters) and :540-544 (full-window tally branches) have no test. t_gated_delta_net.cpp:2778-2824 runs the block path through run_chain_case (:2716-2722): head executor (1 key head per group), finite inputs from recurrence_test_value, and advance() without a tally. The only test that passes a tally to advance() is :2293-2433, with a chain of 3 tokens on the 16 by 80 geometry, and it expects zeros (:2371-2374). t_amx_gdn_numerics.cpp:304-320 calls the kernel directly. So deleting the gdn_recurrence_chain_head call, swapping the two block counters, or deleting line 544 fails no assertion. One correction to the finding: with 1 key head per group, first_head is 0 and value_head equals head_of_key, so the mutation 'pass head_of_key' changes nothing in the only instantiation that production uses (gdn_execution.hpp:104). It matters only for key_heads_per_group > 1, which no production code runs through advance().
verdict.corrected_fix:
Add two executor cases in t_gated_delta_net.cpp at wide_chain_geometry.
(1) Runs on every host: head executor, gdn_block_kernel::off, a tally. 32 tokens from position 0 must give head_tokens[column_half] == 32 and half_full_block_tokens == 32. 33 tokens from position 31 must give head_tokens[column_half] == 33 and half_full_block_tokens == 32 (this also pins the position grid).
(2) Needs AMX (skip otherwise): start_from_checkpoint with +infinity in the matrix of one value head (validate_checkpoint_values rejects only NaN), advance 32 tokens from position 0 with when_available and a tally. Require amx_fallback_blocks == 1, amx_blocks == 1, head_tokens[amx_block] == 32. Require for the refused head the checkpoint rows and output columns of the same run with gdn_block_kernel::off. Use that run as the reference and not step(): it is the same kernel as the fallback, so the compare does not depend on NaN bit patterns. Keep the existing band for the other head.

title: Test comment says the 'small values' family goes below 2^-103; it does not, and no case can detect a wrong loss below 2^-103
problem: Lines 187-189 say that the family with scale 1e-20 'also takes values below 2^-103, where the split drops the bits'. 2^-103 is 9.86e-32. A float64 model of the test with the same generator calls gives for that family: smallest matrix value 3.1e-27, smallest w . Delta value 2.9e-26, and 0 split operands below 2^-103. Only the underflow family passes such operands through the split (14,111 of 32,768 w . Delta values in the model). Their size is about 1e-31 beside sums of about 1, which is far below every bound of the test.
scenario: Change split() so that a value below 2^-103 gets a zero second piece. The relative error of such a value is then up to 2^-8. All 8 families still pass. The design text (section 5.6) lists 'the stated loss below 2^-103' among the tests of the block kernel, and no test covers it.
fix: Correct the comment. Add a family with matrix and value scale near 1e-34 and a bound of its own that follows the stated loss (the unread part of one value is below 2^-126), compared with the float64 result.

verdict.evidence: W = /home/jhan/workspace/ai-runs/tron-gdn-amx-review. W/t/t_amx_gdn_numerics.cpp:187-189 says the 'small values' family takes values below 2^-103. 2^-103 is 9.86e-32. That family draws the matrix and the values as 1e-20 times a standard normal number (lines 198, 212, 94). A draw is below 9.86e-32 only when the normal number is below 9.9e-12 in magnitude, which has a probability of about 8e-12 per value. The second split operand is w . Delta. With decays of 0.9 to 1.0, w is at least 0.9^31 = 0.038, so that operand is not smaller by more than a factor of 26. The split runs only on S0 and on w . Delta (W/src/tron/kernels/amx_gdn.cpp:340-342 and 480-484). So the comment is false whatever the generator gives. I did not rerun the reviewer's float64 model. An estimate from the mean log decay of the underflow family (decay 0.001 to 0.05) gives about 13 of 32 tokens with w . Delta below 2^-103, which agrees with the reported 14,111 of 32,768. Those operands sit beside sums near 1, so the bounds of lines 259-278 cannot see them. Design section 5.6 lists 'the stated loss below 2^-103' among the tests of Part A, and split() is in an unnamed namespace, so no test reaches it.
verdict.corrected_fix:
Correct the comment (lines 187-189): 'The last two families put the start matrix and the values far from 1. Every split operand of the small family is still far above 2^-103, so its three pieces stay exact.'
Then either add a family with state and value scale near 1e-34 with bounds of its own (the third piece of every value is below 2^-126 and is dropped; measure the bounds on the Xeon first, the present 0.2 % and 2e-6 bounds will not hold), or list the missing split-rule test as an open item, because the design promises it.

title: gdn_stats.hpp describes a block grid that advance() does not use
problem: Lines 134-135 say: 'The blocks of a chain are counted from its first token, and that is the grid of half_full_block_tokens.' advance() ends a window where the token position in the sequence reaches a multiple of 32 (gdn_rolling_executor.hpp:514-517). The comment came with the stats commit, and the kernel commit did not update it. Two more statements are inexact. Lines 180-181 give 'a value was not finite' as the only reason for a refusal, and the kernel also refuses a finite correction of 2^100 or more. A refused value head still adds its tokens and its time to the amx path (gdn_rolling_executor.hpp:539-546), while README.stats.md:334-337 says that a path counts the tokens that it advanced.
scenario: Take a chain of 64 tokens that starts at position 16, as after a resume. By the comment it holds 2 full blocks, which is 64 tokens per key head. advance() cuts it into 16 + 32 + 16 tokens and counts 32. A reader who predicts the AMX volume from the chain lengths is wrong by a factor of 2.
fix: Reword lines 134-135: a block starts where the token position in the sequence is a multiple of 32. Reword lines 180-181: refused because a value was not finite or a correction was 2^100 or larger. Add one sentence to README.stats.md: amx_head_tokens includes the windows of refused value heads.

title: layout_of reaches the scratch object without std::launder
problem: reinterpret_cast<scratch_layout*>(scratch.bytes) gives a pointer to the first std::byte. It does not point to the scratch_layout object that C++20 creates implicitly inside the byte array. Access through it needs std::launder ([ptr.launder]). The executor of the same change uses std::launder for its cast of a byte destination (gdn_rolling_executor.hpp:570-573).
scenario: No wrong code is expected from clang or gcc today: every access goes through float or uint16_t lvalues and through intrinsics. The rule is broken on paper only, and the file differs from the convention next to it.
fix: return *std::launder(reinterpret_cast<scratch_layout*>(scratch.bytes)); and add #include <new>.

verdict.evidence: W = /home/jhan/workspace/ai-runs/tron-gdn-amx-review. W/src/tron/kernels/amx_gdn.cpp:121-125 returns *reinterpret_cast<scratch_layout*>(scratch.bytes) with no std::launder, and the file does not include <new> (lines 5-13). The rule is the repository's own: W/h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:1538-1540 says 'A plain cast would still point at the byte, not at the kv_block that lives there ([expr.static.cast], [basic.life], [ptr.launder])', and W/h/tron/models/gdn_rolling_executor.hpp:570-573 uses std::launder for the same kind of cast. scratch_layout (lines 84-116) holds only arrays of uint16_t and float, so it is an implicit-lifetime type and the launder form is valid. No failure is expected from clang or gcc. Style only, lowest priority.
